summary: Add bearer JWT auth so a mobile client can call the API without cookies. POST /login returns an access token; authenticate_user reads Authorization: Bearer.

steps.title: Issue and verify JWTs
steps.description: HS256 JWTs with a 15-minute exp, signed with a local secret. Sub claim is user_id. No refresh token in v1.
steps.rationale: u2 must: bearer JWT; tokens expire in 15 minutes. Local secret keeps us off external IdPs.

steps.title: authenticate_user from the Bearer header
steps.description: def authenticate_user(request) -> User | None. Parses Authorization, verifies the JWT, loads the user. Ignore cookies.
steps.rationale: Same function name as a1, different input. This is the merge conflict waiting to happen.

steps.title: POST /login returns a token in JSON
steps.description: login checks src/users.py and returns {"access_token", "token_type": "bearer", "expires_in": 900}. /health stays open.
steps.rationale: u2 want: POST /login returns the token in JSON for the mobile client.

assumptions: PyJWT is acceptable if it is already in requirements.txt; otherwise hmac+json in stdlib.
Browser cookie sessions are out of scope for u2's must-haves.
